topics.title: Numbers up to 10 000

objectives.text: Name and write numbers up to 10 000
Determine the place value and digit value of a number
Compare and order numbers up to 10 000

topics.offlineActivity: Play 'Bank Teller' with paper notes of RM1000, RM100, RM10 and RM1. Say a number like 3 406 and let him build it with the notes.

lesson.text: Every digit in a number lives in a **house**. The house tells us how much the digit is worth. This is called **place value** (nilai tempat).
Four thousand, seven hundred and twenty-five
A zero is a placeholder. In **3 062** there are **no** hundreds, so we write 0 in the hundreds house.
To compare numbers, look at the **biggest** place first. 5 400 is bigger than 5 040 because 4 hundreds > 0 hundreds.

questions.prompt: What is the place value of 7 in 4 725?
questions.explain: 7 sits in the hundreds house, so it is worth 700.

questions.prompt: Which number is 'six thousand and eight'?
The digit value of 9 in 9 130 is 9 000.
Which number is the biggest?
Arrange from smallest to biggest.
What number comes just after 4 999?
Match the number to its words.

pairs.right: one thousand two hundred and four
one thousand four hundred and twenty

topics.title: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide

objectives.text: Add and subtract numbers within 10 000
Multiply using the 6, 7, 8 and 9 times tables
Divide using the 6, 7, 8 and 9 times tables
Solve daily problems involving the four operations

topics.offlineActivity: Cook together! Ask: 'We need 3 eggs for one cake. How many eggs for 4 cakes?' Let him count the real eggs.

lesson.text: Multiplying can swap: **3 × 6** is the same as **6 × 3**. Both are 18!
18 sweets shared equally among 3 friends. Each friend gets **6**.
Start from the **ones**. 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 to the tens.

questions.prompt: Aina has 1 250 stickers. Her mother gives her 480 more. How many stickers does she have now?
A shop had 3 000 balloons. It sold 1 275. How many are left?
There are 7 boxes. Each box has 8 pencils. How many pencils altogether?
45 durians are shared equally among 9 families. How many durians does each family get?
Fill in the missing numbers.

topics.title: Fractions, Decimals & Percent

objectives.text: Name and write proper fractions with denominators up to 10
Name and write decimals up to one decimal place
Name and write percentages

topics.offlineActivity: Share a pizza or roti canai. Cut it into 4 or 8 equal parts and ask what fraction each person gets.

lesson.text: A pizza is cut into **4 equal parts**. You eat **3** parts. You ate **three quarters** of the pizza.
One tenth can be written as a fraction or a decimal.
**100%** means the whole thing. Half is **50%**.

questions.prompt: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. Ali eats 3 slices. What fraction did he eat?
Match the fraction with its name.
Which decimal is the same as 7/10?
50% is the same as one half.
Which fraction is bigger?
questions.explain: When the top numbers are the same, the smaller bottom number gives bigger pieces.

questions.prompt: 25 out of 100 marbles are red. What percent are red?

topics.title: Money up to RM1000

objectives.text: Represent money value up to RM1000
Add and subtract money up to RM1000
Solve daily problems involving money

topics.offlineActivity: At the pasar or kedai runcit, let him hand over the money and check the change is correct.

lesson.text: **RM1 = 100 sen**. We write RM5 and 50 sen as **RM5.50**.
Line up the **decimal points** when adding or subtracting money.

questions.prompt: How many sen are in RM3?
A shirt costs RM35 and a cap costs RM12. How much altogether? (RM)
You pay RM50 for a toy that costs RM37. What is your change?
RM4.50 is the same as 450 sen.
Can you buy it with RM10?

topics.title: Time

objectives.text: Read and write time in hours and minutes
Know the relationship between units of time

topics.offlineActivity: Give him a real clock at home. Ask him to tell you when it is 'half past 7' before dinner.

lesson.text: **Half past** means 30 minutes after the hour. **Quarter past** means 15 minutes after.

questions.prompt: How many minutes are in 2 hours?
Half past 7 is…
Match the units.
School starts at 7:30 a.m. and recess is at 10:00 a.m. How many minutes is that?
Put the months in order.

topics.title: Length, Mass & Volume

objectives.text: Measure length in cm, m and mm
Measure mass in g and kg
Measure volume of liquid in ml and l

topics.offlineActivity: Use a measuring tape and a kitchen scale. Guess, then measure: how long is the sofa? How heavy is a bag of rice?

lesson.text: Heavy things like a watermelon use **kg**. Light things like a pencil use **g**.

questions.prompt: Would you measure it in g or kg?
Which is the best unit to measure water in a bathtub?
1 l is more than 500 ml.

topics.title: Shapes & Space

objectives.text: Identify 2D shapes and their properties
Identify 3D shapes and their properties

topics.offlineActivity: Go on a 'shape hunt' around the house: find a cylinder, a cube, a cone and a sphere.

questions.prompt: Match the object to its 3D shape.
How many sides does a triangle have?
Which shape has no corners?
A cube has 6 flat faces.
Flat (2D) or solid (3D)?

topics.title: Coordinates, Ratio & Proportion

objectives.text: State the position of an object using coordinates (horizontal, then vertical)
Describe one-to-many ratio
Solve proportion problems (one-to-many)

topics.offlineActivity: Draw a treasure map on grid paper. Hide a sweet at (3, 2) — he must move right 3, then up 2 to find it.

lesson.text: To read a **coordinate**, move **across** (horizontal) first, then **up** (vertical). The treasure at **(4, 2)** is 4 steps across and 2 steps up.
Remember: **walk across the corridor, then go up the stairs!**
This is **proportion** (kadaran): every time we add 1 car, we add 4 wheels.

questions.prompt: The treasure is 3 steps across and 5 steps up. What is its coordinate?
For coordinate (2, 6), we move up 2 first.
1 spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 3 spiders have?
1 box has 6 eggs. How many boxes hold 30 eggs?
1 bicycle : 2 wheels. How many wheels do 5 bicycles have?

topics.title: Data Handling

objectives.text: Read and interpret information in pictographs and bar charts

topics.offlineActivity: Make a tally chart of the colours of cars you see on the way to school. Which colour wins?

questions.prompt: Each 🍎 = 2 apples. Mei Ling has 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does she have?
Each ⭐ = 5 stars. Kavin has ⭐⭐⭐. How many stars?
In a bar chart, the tallest bar shows the biggest number.

topics.title: Scientific Skills

objectives.text: Use science process skills: observe, classify, measure & use numbers, infer, predict, communicate

topics.offlineActivity: Mystery bag: put 5 objects in a bag. He must observe using touch only, then predict what each one is before looking.

lesson.text: Scientists use **process skills** to find out about the world.

rows: Give a reason for what you see
Share results with tables, charts or words

lesson.text: An **inference** is a smart reason. The grass is wet → it probably **rained** last night.

questions.prompt: Match the skill to the example.

pairs.right: The flower is red and smells sweet
The ice will melt in the sun

questions.prompt: The road is wet. 'It rained last night.' Which skill is this?
Which sense do you use to know the durian smells strong?
Drawing a bar chart of your results is 'communicating'.

topics.title: Science Room Rules

objectives.text: Follow the rules of the science room

topics.offlineActivity: Make a 'Safety First' poster together for the kitchen: no running, wash hands, ask before touching hot things.

items: Keep the room clean and tidy

lesson.text: If something breaks, **tell your teacher** — don't pick up broken glass yourself!

questions.prompt: Safe or unsafe in the science room?
A test tube breaks. What should you do?
You may enter the science room without a teacher.

topics.title: Humans: Our Teeth

objectives.text: Know milk teeth and permanent teeth
Identify types of teeth and their functions
Know the structure of a tooth
Practise correct dental care

topics.offlineActivity: Brush teeth together in front of a mirror. Count his teeth and spot the incisors, canines and molars. Check for wobbly milk teeth!

lesson.text: Brush **twice a day**, floss, eat fewer sweets and visit the dentist every **6 months**.

questions.prompt: Match the tooth to its job.
How many milk teeth does a child have?
How many permanent teeth does an adult have?
Which is the hardest part of a tooth?
Good or bad for your teeth?
Complete the sentence.
questions.text: The ___ has nerves and blood vessels. The ___ hold the teeth in place.

topics.title: Animals

objectives.text: Group animals by body covering and how they reproduce
Classify animals by eating habits: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore
Relate the teeth of animals to what they eat

topics.offlineActivity: Visit Zoo Negara, an aquarium or a farm. At each animal ask: What covers its body? Does it lay eggs? What does it eat?

questions.prompt: Drag each animal to the right group.
Match the animal to its body covering.
Lays eggs or gives birth?
A tiger has long, sharp canines. What does it eat?
A chicken eats grains and worms. It is a…

topics.title: Plants

objectives.text: Know the different ways plants reproduce
Explain why plant reproduction is important

topics.offlineActivity: Grow kangkung from seeds and a stem cutting side by side (like in the textbook). Compare which grows faster over two weeks.

lesson.text: How do plants make new plants?
Scientists can grow many plants from a tiny piece using **tissue culture** (kultur tisu).
Plants reproduce so they **don't become extinct** and so humans and animals always have **food**.

questions.prompt: Match the plant to how it reproduces.
How do we usually grow sweet potato (ubi keledek)?
Mushrooms reproduce using…
Plant reproduction helps make sure we have enough food.

topics.title: Measurement: Area & Volume

objectives.text: Measure area using square units
Measure volume using cube units

topics.offlineActivity: Use square sticky notes to cover a book cover, then count them. Build a box shape with Lego cubes and count the cubes for volume.

lesson.text: We can count **cubes** to find the volume of a solid.
Standard units: area in **cm²**, volume in **cm³**.

questions.prompt: A shape is covered by 4 rows of 5 squares. What is its area?
A box is built from 3 layers of 4 cubes. What is its volume?
Which unit is used to measure area?
Volume tells us how much space an object takes up.

topics.title: Density

objectives.text: Relate floating and sinking to density

topics.offlineActivity: Bath-time test: predict, then check if a spoon, a sponge, a coin, an apple and a plastic toy float or sink.

lesson.text: Objects that are **less dense** than water **float**. Objects that are **denser** than water **sink**.
Cooking **oil floats on water** because oil is less dense than water.

questions.prompt: Does it float or sink in water?
Oil is poured into water. Where does the oil go?
An object that is denser than water will sink.

topics.title: Acids & Alkalis

objectives.text: Identify acidic, alkaline and neutral substances using litmus paper

topics.offlineActivity: With adult help, make red-cabbage 'magic water' and add lime juice, then soapy water. Watch the colours change!

items: Acids: lime juice, vinegar, tamarind (asam jawa)

lesson.text: Use **litmus paper** to test — never taste!

questions.prompt: Acid or alkali?
Blue litmus paper turns red. The substance is…
Distilled water does not change either litmus paper. It is…
An alkali turns red litmus paper blue.

topics.title: The Solar System

objectives.text: Name the members of the Solar System and the order of the planets
Know that planets move around the Sun

topics.offlineActivity: Learn the planet order with a silly sentence: 'My Very Excited Mother Just Served Us Nasi-lemak.' Make planets from playdough.

lesson.text: The **Sun** is a star at the centre. **8 planets** move around it in their own paths (orbits).

questions.prompt: Put these planets in order from the Sun.
Which is the biggest planet?
How many planets are in the Solar System?
Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
The Sun moves around the Earth.
questions.explain: The Earth moves around the Sun.

topics.title: Simple Machines

objectives.text: Identify types of simple machines and examples
Know that a complex machine is made of simple machines

topics.offlineActivity: Machine hunt at home: find a lever (scissors), wheel and axle (doorknob), screw (jar lid), wedge (knife) and inclined plane (ramp).

lesson.text: A bicycle is a **complex machine** — it has gears, wheels & axles and levers (brakes)!

questions.prompt: Match the object to its simple machine.
A doorknob is an example of a…
Which is a complex machine?
Simple machines make our work easier.

topics.title: Animals & Habitats

objectives.text: Understand and use vocabulary about animals and habitats

topics.offlineActivity: Watch a nature documentary together and pause to name 5 animals and where they live — in English.

lesson.text: The tiger lives in the jungle.
The **hornbill** is the state bird of Sarawak!

questions.prompt: Match the English word to the Malay word.
Which animal is this?
Where does a fish live?
Complete the sentence.

topics.title: Jobs People Do

objectives.text: Understand and use vocabulary about occupations

topics.offlineActivity: On the way to school, point to people working (police officer, cashier, driver) and ask 'What does he/she do?'

lesson.text: A firefighter puts out fires. A pilot flies an aeroplane.

questions.prompt: Who does what?
Who puts out fires?
Complete the sentence.
questions.text: My mother is a ___. She teaches children at school.

topics.title: Weather & Clothes

objectives.text: Talk about the weather and what to wear

topics.offlineActivity: Each morning, ask him to look outside and say 'It's sunny/rainy/cloudy today, so I'll take…'

lesson.text: It's rainy today. I need my umbrella and raincoat.

questions.prompt: Match the weather.
It's rainy. What should you take?
Sunny day or rainy day?

topics.title: Simple Past Tense

objectives.text: Use the simple past tense of regular and irregular verbs

topics.offlineActivity: At dinner, ask 'What did you do today?' and gently recast his answers into the past tense.

lesson.text: We use the **past tense** for things that already happened. Many verbs just add **-ed**.
Yesterday I went to the park and played football.

questions.prompt: Choose the past tense.
questions.text: Yesterday, I ___ football with my friends.

questions.prompt: Match the verb to its past tense.
Last night, we ___ nasi lemak.
The past tense of 'jump' is 'jumped'.
Fill both blanks.
questions.text: Mei ___ to the zoo and ___ a panda.

topics.title: Prepositions

objectives.text: Use prepositions of place: in, on, under, next to, behind

topics.offlineActivity: Hide a toy and give clues using prepositions: 'It is under something soft, next to the door.'

questions.prompt: The book is ___ the table. (It is on top.)
Complete it.
The ball is ___ the bed. (It is below.)
Build the sentence.

topics.title: Building Sentences

objectives.text: Write simple sentences with correct word order

topics.offlineActivity: Write words on sticky notes and let him build silly sentences on the fridge.

lesson.text: A sentence needs a **who** and a **doing word** (verb).
Start with a **capital letter** and end with a **full stop**.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
Put the words in order.
Build the question.
Which sentence is correct?

topics.title: Reading: A Day at the Farm

objectives.text: Understand the main idea and details of a short text

topics.offlineActivity: Read a short story together at bedtime. Ask 3 questions: who, where, and what happened.

lesson.text: On Saturday, Hana visited her grandfather's farm in Kedah. She fed the **goats** and collected **eggs** from the chickens. In the afternoon, she helped Grandpa pick **rambutans**. Hana was tired but very happy.
On Saturday, Hana visited her grandfather's farm in Kedah. She fed the goats and collected eggs from the chickens. In the afternoon, she helped Grandpa pick rambutans. Hana was tired but very happy.

questions.prompt: When did Hana visit the farm?
What did Hana collect?
The farm is in Johor.
How did Hana feel at the end?

topics.title: Kata Nama

objectives.text: Memahami dan menggunakan kata nama am dan kata nama khas

topics.offlineActivity: Semasa berjalan-jalan, main 'Cari Kata Nama Khas': papan tanda kedai, nama jalan dan nama bandar.

lesson.text: **Kata nama** ialah perkataan yang menamakan orang, haiwan, benda, tempat atau perkara.
Kata nama **khas** sentiasa bermula dengan **huruf besar**.

questions.prompt: Asingkan kata nama am dan kata nama khas.
Antara berikut, yang manakah kata nama khas?
'kucing' ialah kata nama am.

topics.title: Kata Kerja

objectives.text: Memahami dan menggunakan kata kerja dalam ayat

topics.offlineActivity: Main 'Saya Buat, Awak Teka': lakonkan perbuatan (melompat, menyapu, membaca) dan dia teka kata kerjanya.

questions.prompt: Apakah kata kerja dalam ayat ini: 'Ali menendang bola.'
Padankan gambar dengan kata kerja.
Lengkapkan ayat.

topics.title: Kata Adjektif

objectives.text: Memahami dan menggunakan kata adjektif (warna, ukuran, sifat)

topics.offlineActivity: Pilih satu buah (contoh: tembikai). Bergilir-gilir menyebut kata adjektif untuknya: besar, hijau, manis, berat.

lesson.text: **Kata adjektif** menerangkan sifat sesuatu kata nama.

questions.prompt: Warna atau rasa?
Gajah itu sangat ___.
Yang manakah kata adjektif?

topics.title: Imbuhan Awalan

objectives.text: Memahami dan menggunakan imbuhan awalan ber- dan me-

topics.offlineActivity: Tulis kata dasar pada kad (lari, baca, main). Dia tambah 'ber-' atau 'me-' dan bina ayat lisan.

lesson.text: 'me-' boleh berubah menjadi **mem-, men-, meng-, meny-** mengikut huruf pertama kata dasar.

questions.prompt: Pilih perkataan yang betul.
Padankan kata dasar dengan kata terbitan.
Kakak ___ lantai setiap pagi.

topics.title: Simpulan Bahasa

objectives.text: Memahami dan menggunakan simpulan bahasa dengan betul

topics.offlineActivity: Pilih satu simpulan bahasa setiap hari dan cuba gunakan dalam perbualan di rumah.

lesson.text: **Simpulan bahasa** ialah rangkai kata yang membawa maksud yang berbeza daripada makna asalnya.
Adik saya ringan tulang kerana selalu membantu ibu.

questions.prompt: Padankan simpulan bahasa dengan maksudnya.
Amin tidak pandai bermain bola. Dia seorang yang ___.
'Ringan tulang' bermaksud malas.

topics.title: Bina Ayat

objectives.text: Membina dan menulis ayat tunggal dengan betul

topics.offlineActivity: Beri tiga perkataan (contoh: kucing, tidur, sofa). Dia bina satu ayat lengkap secara lisan.

lesson.text: Mulakan dengan **huruf besar** dan akhiri dengan **noktah**.

questions.prompt: Susun perkataan menjadi ayat.
Susun perkataan menjadi ayat.
Susun perkataan menjadi ayat.
